entities.summary: Toribio Alonso de Salazar was a Spanish navigator of Basque origin, who was the first Westerner to arrive on the Marshall Islands on 21 August 1526. Born into a family of sailors and traders, Alonso de Salazar was trained in navigation and cartography from a young age. His experiences as a sailor and explorer shaped his understanding of the Pacific Ocean and its many islands. Alonso de Salazar's voyage to the Marshall Islands was part of a larger expedition to explore the Pacific and establish trade routes. He was commissioned by King Charles I of Spain to lead an expedition to the Pacific and to search for the legendary Island of Bora Bora. Alonso de Salazar's discovery of the Marshall Islands marked a significant milestone in the history of Spanish exploration and trade in the Pacific. His voyage also had a profound impact on the indigenous populations of the Marshall Islands, who had never seen Europeans before. Alonso de Salazar's legacy extends beyond his own voyage, as he paved the way for future Spanish explorers and traders to explore and settle the Pacific. He is remembered as a pioneering navigator and explorer who played a significant role in shaping the history of the Pacific Islands.
